newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says Ok Tedi copper barges halted.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says Ok Tedi copper barges halted.

text.p: Shipments of concentrates down the Fly River by barge from the Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea have been halted since last week by low water levels, with deliveries being met from stockpiles, the mine's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Thursday.
"It's been about a week since shipments have been able to get through," BHP spokesman, Vincent Bull, told Reuters by telephone from Port Moresby.
Bull said so far there have been sufficient stockpiles amassed in a transhipment vessl in the Gulf of Papua to meet delivery schedules.
However, Bull could not say how much concentrate was still on hand at the silo.
"Obviously at some point it would run out, but when is another question," Bull said.
It was not uncommon this time of year for the water level of the river to fall to a level where shipments must be postponed, Bull said.
Ok Tedi produces about 600,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually, Bull said. The material is typically shipped to destinations in Asia and Europe, he added.

Concentrates are transported by pipeline from the mine to the port of Kiunga, and then by barge down the Fly River for loading onto a silo vessel in the Gulf of Papua before being transferred to waiting bulk freighters.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp, with 17.4 percent and the Papua New Guinea government 30 percent.
